screening_decisions.reason: RCT of elderly depressed outpatients who had responded to antidepressants and completed continuation therapy, randomised to maintenance treatment with nortriptyline, phenelzine, or placebo. Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.
This is a scale development/validation study, not an RCT examining maintenance treatment for depression. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a psychometric validation study of a therapist competence scale, not an RCT examining maintenance treatment for depression. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a narrative review article, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a systematic review using NNT analysis, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis examining risk factors, not an RCT examining maintenance treatment. Does not meet study design criteria.

While this is a follow-up of an RCT examining CBT for relapse prevention, the abstract does not specify that participants were aged 60+. The study appears to include general adult populations without age restriction. Cannot confirm age criterion met.

RCT of people aged 65+ living in the community who were openly treated with sertraline then randomised to double-blind placebo-controlled continuation/maintenance study. Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.
This is a review article examining cognitive effects, not an RCT examining maintenance treatment. Does not meet study design criteria.

RCT of persons aged 70+ with major depression who met criteria for recovery and entered maintenance treatment, randomised to paroxetine vs placebo and interpersonal psychotherapy vs clinical management. Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.

Pilot RCT of adults aged 60+ who had met ICD-10 criteria for major depression in the previous year, randomised to CBT-G/antidepressant combination or antidepressant alone. Meets all criteria: age 60+, recently depressed, RCT design, maintenance/recurrence prevention treatment.
This is a conceptual paper proposing definitions for remission, recovery, relapse, and recurrence. Not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.

RCT of elderly patients with histories of recurrent major depression, randomly assigned to 3-year double-blind maintenance pharmacotherapy with nortriptyline at different plasma levels. Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.

RCT of out-patients aged 65+ with unipolar major depression who responded to citalopram treatment, then randomised to double-blind citalopram or placebo for at least 48 weeks. Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.

While this is an RCT examining maintenance treatment for recurrent depression, the abstract does not specify that participants were aged 60+. The study appears to include general outpatient populations without age restriction. Cannot confirm age criterion met.
This is an instrument development/reliability study for a diagnostic interview schedule, not an RCT examining maintenance treatment. Does not meet study design criteria.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques in cancer studies, not an RCT examining depression maintenance treatment. Does not meet any criteria.

While this is an RCT comparing MBCT with maintenance antidepressants for relapse prevention, the abstract specifies 'adult patients' without indicating age 60+. The study recruited from general practices without age restriction mentioned. Cannot confirm age criterion met.

RCT of patients 70 years of age or older with major depression who responded to initial treatment with paroxetine and psychotherapy, then randomised to four maintenance-treatment programs (paroxetine/placebo x psychotherapy/clinical-management). Meets all criteria: age 60+, successfully treated, RCT design, maintenance treatment.
This is a systematic overview of evidence from randomised trials, not an RCT itself. Does not meet study design criteria.

This is a two-year maintenance RCT comparing monthly maintenance IPT vs supportive clinical management in remitted depressed elderly patients. The study explicitly states participants were 'remitted depressed elderly' who had completed prior treatment. The intervention is maintenance psychological therapy (IPT) which falls within the selection criteria. Population is elderly (60+), they were successfully treated for depression, and randomized to maintenance treatment.

This is a review article discussing psychotherapy for depression in older people. The abstract mentions 'evidence...comes from a limited number of randomised controlled trials' indicating it reviews existing trials rather than being an RCT itself. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is a Cochrane review (indicated by cochranelibrary.com reference) examining efficacy of antidepressant classes. It is a systematic review, not a primary RCT. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is an observational population-based study using administrative database to examine antidepressant prescribing patterns. No randomization or intervention. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is an RCT where 58 elderly subjects remitted from major depression received continuation nortriptyline for 16 weeks, then were randomly assigned to nortriptyline maintenance therapy or placebo for up to 2 years. Meets all criteria: elderly population (60+), successfully treated for depression (remitted), randomized to maintenance treatment (antidepressant).

This appears to be a review article (references 'reviews advocating psychotherapy'). The abstract is incomplete but indicates it's examining evidence from existing trials rather than conducting a new RCT. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a community-based, prospective, observational study examining the relationship between depressive symptoms and functional disability. No randomization or intervention. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is a systematic literature review with expert panel assessment of community-based interventions. Not a primary RCT. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled maintenance trial with 130 older adults aged 65+ with recently remitted major depression. Participants were randomized to maintenance antidepressant pharmacotherapy plus donepezil or plus placebo. Meets all criteria: elderly (65+), successfully treated (recently remitted), randomized to maintenance treatment (antidepressant).

This is about recruitment strategies for a dietary intervention trial exploring diet and immune function. The intervention is dietary, not antidepressant or psychological therapy for depression. Does not meet the intervention criteria.

This is a 2x2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients older than 59 years (average age 67). 107 patients were fully recovered after acute treatment and continuation, then randomized to 4 maintenance therapy conditions (nortriptyline, IPT, combination, or placebo). Meets all criteria: elderly (60+), successfully treated (fully recovered), randomized to maintenance treatment (antidepressant and/or psychological therapy).
This is a methodological paper describing a rating scale for depression. Not an RCT. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

While this is an RCT in older people (65+) with depression, it tests acute treatment effectiveness (CBT vs TAU vs talking control) in people WITH depression, not maintenance treatment in people who were SUCCESSFULLY TREATED for an episode of depression. The selection criteria specifically requires participants to be 'successfully treated for an episode of depression' before randomization to maintenance treatment. This study randomizes people with active depression to treatment, not remitted people to maintenance.
This is a methodological paper developing a therapy rating scale to discriminate between maintenance treatments. Not an RCT testing treatment efficacy. Does not meet the RCT requirement.
